problem: Existing video benchmarks are limited to simple scene-level queries or global summaries, lacking evaluation of multi-hop multimodal reasoning needed for real-world video understanding.
method: Introduces AgentVidBench, a multi-hop video question answering benchmark that provides step-by-step solution traces to support trajectory evaluation, assessing whether agents acquire evidence needed to justify answers.
key_assumptions: Step-by-step solution traces can effectively evaluate multimodal reasoning trajectories.
Integrating MLLMs into agentic workflows improves performance on complex video understanding.
main_contribution: AgentVidBench benchmark and datasets/code for evaluating MLLM agents on spatial, temporal, and causal reasoning in video understanding, showing that agentic workflows improve performance over single-turn MLLMs.
baselines: simple agentic strategy as competitive baseline
results: ["Single-turn MLLM performance limited; integrating into agentic workflows improves accuracy and trajectory scores."]

relation_to_idea.conceptual_difference: AgentVidBench focuses on video QA benchmarking with step-by-step traces, while the idea targets KGQA via context subgraph enrichment, adaptive repair loop, and RL transfer.
